final_rationale: The verdict does not change because the Actor provided no genuinely new admissible evidence; the response is a narrower interpretation of the same record. That narrower framing is useful but it does not close the initial concerns. Public governance guidance and aggregate readiness evidence support a limited argument that launch readiness is not broadly failing, but they do not substitute for the release-policy requirement that material limitations for named launch use cases be disclosed unless resolved or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch. The Actor expressly concedes there is no admissible evidence of completed disclosure, no approved risk acceptance, and no final legal determination. That means the proposed caveat is not merely a qualifier on an otherwise compliant record; it is itself an unresolved compliance condition. On this record, certification may be arguable only if disclosure is actually completed or approved risk acceptance exists before launch, but current compliance is still not evidentially established.
remaining_concerns: The pharmacy prior authorization segment still misses target by 1.2 percentage points and is named in two payer pilot commitments, so the weakness remains potentially material under the provided policy text.
